NETWORKING · HISTORICAL SETUP

Cloud-to-Home Reverse Proxy

A cloud entry point connected to home-hosted applications through a Newt tunnel.

AWS EC2PangolinNewtCloudflareTraefik

System at a glance

Cloudflare→AWS EC2 / Pangolin→Newt tunnel→Home services

What I built

  • Hosted Pangolin on AWS EC2 and connected the home network through Newt.
  • Worked on routing to Proxmox, AMP, and a Next.js application.
  • Investigated the ongoing cost of the cloud endpoint after AWS credits, including local alternatives. Current hosting status needs an update.

Troubleshooting notes

Proxmox upstream TLS

The Proxmox backend uses HTTPS on port 8006. Turning off upstream TLS led to a gateway timeout during troubleshooting.

Proxy routing

Worked through Traefik routers, upstream protocols, and certificate handling across several network hops.

What I learned

  • A tunnel and a reverse proxy handle different parts of the request path.
  • Trace DNS, the public endpoint, tunnel connectivity, and backend reachability one hop at a time.
Documentation compiled from my project notes and shared troubleshooting history. Commands, final configuration files, and screenshots will be added as they are verified. The diagram is a simplified project overview.
